column3: The timeline anchors the scrolled-up view itself (first visible item, restored scrollTop rounded) and turns native overflow-anchor off
column4: Chrome's native anchoring moved a scrolled-up view by 1px with no resize in the timeline (scrollTop set to 200 read 199 a moment later in 4 of 10 probe runs), which XIN-23 saw as a flaky e2e test; content sits on fractional pixels, so a native adjustment can land a pixel off
column5: A probe logged every scrollTop write and ResizeObserver entry: no product write and no resize preceded the 200 to 199 move; with own anchoring 10 of 10 probe rounds held 200 and the e2e test passed 10 of 10
